newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen consolidating after rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen consolidating after rise.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee futures could move sideways with second-month September consolidating its recent gains above $1,600 a tonne, traders said on Wednesday.
The market was due to open $20 lower after New York futures finished with pared gains on Tuesday on overhead origin selling and light profit-taking.
Robusta futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday but left a chart gap between $1,619 and $1,650 on September unfilled.
Traders said some buying could emerge if the market hit the $1,619 support on the way down.
Initial resistance is pegged at $1,700, followed by a layer of barriers at around $1,720-$1,750 -- the lows seen in June.
On balance, they said the market was still in a consolidative phase as it built a strong base at above $1,600.
The 14-day relative strength indicator was neutral at 47 percent but short- and medium-term moving averages showed a downward trend.

In other news, members of Brazil's coffee council, known as the CDPC, would hold another preliminary meeting in Brasilia Thursday ahead of its next formal session, a spokeswoman for the Industry and Commerce Ministry (MICT) said.
Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the MICT, declined to discuss any specific issues following a meeting of council members earlier Tuesday.

He declined to comment on whether a government plan to lend stocks to the soluble industry, which has been complaining about difficulty in obtaining raw material, would go ahead amid market rumours that the project had been scrapped.
Soluble industry officials were not immediately available to comment on talk that they plan to import robusta coffee from India under a drawback regime instead to alleviate the supply problems.
Elsewhere, the Brazilian government is to auction 85,800 60-kg bags of coffee from its stocks at regular monthly auction on August 6.
In Singapore, traders said Vietnam could overtake Indonesia as Asia's largest coffee exporter in the 1997/98 season.
